mainTopic: Liquids from impure sources (a זב versus a מת), and the laws of כיסוי הדם: which blood must be covered and with what materials
overview: The גמרא finishes a teaching about liquids that come out of a טבול יום and out of other impure sources. It explains that 'major' sources means a זב, not a מת. It also explains why the רבנן made a גזירה about liquids from a זב but not from a מת: people stay away from a corpse on their own. Then the גמרא turns to כיסוי הדם. Two ברייתות discuss blood that spurted or stayed on the knife, and the גמרא shows that the רבנן, רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל each read the word 'דמו' differently. A new משנה lists which materials may be used to cover the blood: fine, earth-like material, or in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words, anything plants can grow in. The גמרא defines 'fine sand' with a potter test, in two versions, and shows how the versions differ. Finally, a ברייתא learns from 'בעפר' that stones and an upside-down vessel are not allowed. It begins asking which other fine materials are included, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Liquids from a טבול יום versus liquids from other impure sources
steps.stepSummary: Liquids that come out of a טבול יום, and liquids he touches, do not make things impure. Liquids that come out of any other impure source count the same as liquids that touched it: they are ראשון לטומאה. The exception is a liquid that is itself an אב הטומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both kinds of liquid (what comes out of a טבול יום and what he touches) do not make things impure. For all other impure sources, minor or major, liquids that come out of them are like liquids that touch them. Both are first-degree impure, except a liquid that is itself a primary source of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quoted teaching that compares liquids coming out of an impure person to liquids that touch him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טבול יום is a weak kind of impurity, so nothing that comes from him or touches him passes on impurity. With every other impure source, a liquid that comes out of the body is treated as if it touched the source, so it becomes a תחילה. The words 'minor or major' will be examined in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who went to the מקוה today but must wait for nightfall to be fully pure
Liquids that come out of a person's body
First-degree impurity (ראשון לטומאה)
A primary source of impurity

phrases.english: And both these and those do not impart impurity,
phrases.notes: 'These and those' are the liquids that come out of a טבול יום and the liquids he touches.

phrases.english: And all other impure sources,
whether minor or major —
liquids that come out of them
are like liquid that touches them,
and both these and those are first-degree impure,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִן הַמַּשְׁקֶה שֶׁהוּא אַב הַטּוּמְאָה.
phrases.english: except for a liquid that is itself a primary source of impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a teaching that the גמרא was already quoting before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liquids from a טבול יום do not make things impure. Liquids from all other impure sources are a תחילה, like liquids that touched them, except a liquid that is itself an אב הטומאה.

steps.title: Does 'major' mean a corpse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'minor' and 'major' mean. It suggests that 'major' means a מת. That reading would clash with the earlier rule that liquids from a corpse are pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are 'minor' and what are 'major'? Isn't it that 'minor' means a שרץ and a זב, and 'major' means a מת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'minor' and 'major' sources mean. It offers the obvious reading, which would cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מת is the most severe impurity, so 'major' seems to mean a corpse. Then this teaching would say liquids from a corpse are impure. That contradicts the earlier teaching that liquids from a מת are pure, except blood. The question is really a hidden challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Minor (lighter) sources of impurity
Major (more severe) sources of impurity
A dead creeping creature that is impure
A man who is impure because of an unusual discharge
A human corpse, the most severe impurity

phrases.english: What are 'minor' and what are 'major'?
Is it not that 'minor' means a creeping creature and a זב,
and 'major' means a corpse?
phrases.notes: If so, this would clash with the earlier teaching that liquids coming out of a corpse are pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קַלִּין וּמַאי חֲמוּרִין? מַאי לָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the words 'minor or major' in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier rule that liquids from a מת are pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'major' means a מת, this teaching says liquids from a corpse are impure, which contradicts the earlier teaching.

steps.title: 'Major' means a זב
steps.stepSummary: No. 'Minor' means a שרץ, and 'major' means a זב. A מת is not included at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'Minor' means a שרץ, and 'major' means a זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'major' refers to a זב, not a מת, so there is no contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the teaching never talks about a corpse. So the earlier rule that liquids from a מת are pure stays in place. Liquids that come out of a זב are impure.

phrases.english: No: 'minor' means a creeping creature,
and 'major' means a זב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 2 by reading the words differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Major' means a מת, so liquids from a corpse would be impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Major' means a זב. The teaching says nothing about a מת, so liquids from a corpse stay pure.

steps.title: Why a גזירה for a זב but not for a מת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן made a גזירה about liquids from a זב but not about liquids from a מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a זב, that the רבנן made a גזירה about him, and what is different about a מת, that the רבנן did not make a גזירה about it?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the rule is stricter for a זב, the גמרא asks why. A corpse is the more severe impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You would expect the רבנן to be stricter with a מת, which is the heaviest impurity. Yet they made a גזירה only for a זב. The גמרא wants the reason for this surprising difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
The רבנן made a rabbinic decree (גזירה)

phrases.english: What is different about a זב,
that the Rabbis made a decree about him,
and what is different about a corpse
that the Rabbis did not make a decree about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא זָב, דִּגְזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the conclusion of Step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the רבנן were stricter with liquids from a זב than with liquids from a מת

steps.title: People stay away from a corpse but not from a זב
steps.stepSummary: People don't naturally stay away from a זב, so the רבנן needed a גזירה. People already stay away from a מת on their own, so no גזירה was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A זב, whom people don't keep away from, the רבנן made a גזירה about. A מת, which people do keep away from, the רבנן did not make a גזירה about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the גזירה depends on how people act. Rules were added only where people would otherwise come into contact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב walks around among people, so they could easily touch liquids coming from him. The רבנן made a fence to protect them. With a corpse, people already keep their distance, so a fence was not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: People keep away from him or it

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן made a גזירה that all liquids coming out of a זב are impure. Liquids from a מת (except blood) are pure. The reason is that people stay away from a corpse on their own, but not from a זב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common pattern: the רבנן add a גזירה where people are likely to slip, not just where the impurity is most severe.

phrases.english: A זב, whom people don't keep away from —
the Rabbis made a decree about him;
a corpse, which people keep away from —
the Rabbis did not make a decree about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן made a גזירה where people don't naturally separate (a זב), and not where they already do (a מת).

steps.title: Blood that spurted or stayed on the knife must be covered
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: the גמרא quotes the משנה about blood that spurted or stayed on the knife. A ברייתא learns from 'וכסהו' that this blood must also be covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Blood that spurts and that is on the knife': the רבנן taught, 'And he shall cover it' teaches that blood that spurted and blood on the knife must be covered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes words from the משנה about כיסוי הדם and brings a ברייתא that gives the source in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the blood is covered in the place where the animal was slaughtered. The ברייתא learns from the word 'וכסהו' that blood that sprayed away, or stuck to the knife, also needs covering.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood that spurted away during slaughter
'And he shall cover it', the פסוק commanding כיסוי הדם
Obligated to cover

phrases.english: 'Blood that spurts and that is on the knife':
The Rabbis taught: 'And he shall cover it' —
teaches that blood that spurted
and blood on the knife must be covered.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּם הַנִּיתָּז וְשֶׁעַל הַסַּכִּין, תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Switches from impurity of liquids to a new topic, כיסוי הדם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood that spurted, or that is on the knife, must be covered. This is learned from 'וכסהו'.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only when there is no other blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה limits the rule. Spurted blood or blood on the knife must be covered only when no other blood is there. If other blood is there, there is no obligation to cover it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When does this apply? When there is no blood there except this blood. But if there is other blood there, he is exempt from covering it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a limit to the ברייתא's rule about spurted blood and blood on the knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, this leftover blood needs covering only when it is all the blood there is. If the main blood is also there to be covered, the spurted blood or blood on the knife is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: When? (introducing a limit on a rule)
Exempt from covering

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not arguing that spurted blood never needs covering. He is only limiting the obligation to cases where no other blood is there.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: When does this apply?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין שָׁם דָּם אֶלָּא הוּא,
phrases.english: When there is no blood there except that blood,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ שָׁם דָּם שֶׁלֹּא הוּא –
phrases.english: but if there is blood there other than that blood —
he is exempt from covering it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on the rule of Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spurted blood or blood on the knife must be covered only when no other blood is there. Otherwise, there is no obligation to cover it.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: all the blood must be covered
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא learns from 'וכסהו' that all the blood must be covered, including spurted blood and blood on the sides of the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'And he shall cover it' teaches that all the blood must be covered. So the חכמים said that blood that spurted out, and blood on the sides of the neck, must be covered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that starts with the same basic rule we saw before: all the blood must be covered. It is setting up a new opinion, from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of this ברייתא matches the earlier ברייתא from Step 6. It adds 'blood on the sides' (of the neck) to 'spurted blood' as blood that still must be covered. The new point of this ברייתא is the limit that follows in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The sides of the animal's neck where it was slaughtered

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
"And he shall cover it" teaches
that one must cover all of its blood.
From here they said:
Blood that spurted out, and blood that is on the sides of the neck,
one must cover it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא to Step 6, which will lead to a different limiting opinion than רבי יהודה's in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'וכסהו', all the blood must be covered, including spurted blood and blood on the sides of the neck.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits the rule to when the main blood was not covered
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says spurted blood must be covered only if the main 'blood of the soul' was not covered. If it was covered, there is no obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: When does this rule apply? When the person did not cover the דם הנפש. But if he did cover the דם הנפש, he does not have to cover the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a limit to the rule we just read. The extra blood must be covered only if the main blood was not covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה (Step 7) made the rule depend on whether any other blood is there. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל makes it depend on the דם הנפש specifically. Once the דם הנפש is covered, the מצוה is done, and the rest of the blood does not need to be covered.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When is this said?' – a phrase that introduces a limit on a rule
'Blood of the soul' – the main blood that flows out as the animal dies
Exempt; there is no obligation

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
When is this statement said?
When he did not cover the blood of the soul.
phrases.notes: This means the main blood that pours out while the animal dies.

phrases.english: But if he did cover the blood of the soul,
he is exempt from covering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of the ברייתא in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spurted blood must be covered only if the דם הנפש was not covered; once the דם הנפש is covered, there is no obligation.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the three opinions are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the real reason is behind the three different opinions. It is setting up the answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now have three views: the רבנן (always cover spurted blood), רבי יהודה (only if no other blood is there), and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (only if the דם הנפש was not covered). The גמרא wants to find the one point that makes them differ.

keyTerms.meaning: About what?
Are they disagreeing

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the three opinions from Steps 6-9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basic point that divides the רבנן, רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Three ways to read the word 'דמו'
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement depends on how each one reads 'דמו' (its blood): all of it, even some of it, or the special blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold 'דמו' means all of its blood. רבי יהודה holds 'דמו' means even some of its blood. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds 'דמו' means the special blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: all three opinions come from reading the one word 'דמו' in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, 'דמו' means every drop, so spurted blood must always be covered. For רבי יהודה, even some of the blood is enough, so if other blood is there to cover, the spurted blood can be left. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, 'דמו' means the special blood, the דם הנפש, so once that is covered the מצוה is done.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Its blood' – the word in the פסוק they all read differently
All of its blood
Some; a part
The special one; here, the main blood (דם הנפש)
Holds; is of the opinion

steps.whatToRemember: One word, three readings: the רבנן say 'all of it', רבי יהודה says 'even part of it', and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says 'the special blood' (דם הנפש).

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: "Its blood" means all of its blood.
Rabbi Yehuda holds: "Its blood" means
even part of its blood.
And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
"Its blood" means the special blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree on the word 'דמו': all of the blood (רבנן), even part of it (רבי יהודה), or the special blood, the דם הנפש (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל).

steps.title: משנה: what may and may not be used to cover the blood
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists fine materials that may be used for covering, and coarse or uncrushed materials, or an upside-down vessel, that may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: With what may one cover, and with what may one not cover? One may cover with fine manure, fine sand, lime, crushed pottery, and a brick or barrel lid that was crushed. But one may not cover with coarse manure, coarse sand, or a brick or lid that was not crushed. And one may not just turn a vessel upside down over the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins a new topic: which materials are good for covering the blood. It gives a list of allowed and not-allowed materials.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is that fine, crumbly material is allowed, and coarse or solid material is not. The same brick or lid can be allowed or not allowed, depending only on whether it was crushed. Turning a vessel over the blood is not allowed, because the blood itself has not been covered with material.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין – our משנה
Manure
Lime (a white powder)
Crushed pottery
A brick
A clay lid of a barrel

steps.confusionAlert: The brick and the lid show up on both lists. That is not a mistake: crushed, they are allowed; whole, they are not.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
With what may one cover, and with what may one not cover?
One may cover with fine manure, and with fine sand,
with lime, and with crushed pottery,
and with a brick or a barrel lid that one crushed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין מְכַסִּין לֹא בְּזֶבֶל הַגַּס,
phrases.english: But one may not cover with coarse manure,
nor with coarse sand,
nor with a brick or a barrel lid that one did not crush.
And one may not turn a vessel upside down over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic: the materials used for covering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fine or crushed materials may be used to cover the blood; coarse or uncrushed materials, or an upside-down vessel, may not.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's general rule: anything plants grow in
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a general rule: a material that plants can grow in may be used for covering; one that plants cannot grow in may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל stated a general rule: anything that plants grow in, one may cover with it. Anything that plants do not grow in, one may not cover with it.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of a list, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives one simple test for every material: can plants grow in it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list sorted materials by fine or coarse. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives one test that explains which materials pass: they must be like soil, something plants can grow in.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
Grows; lets things grow
Plants

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's main idea: cover the blood with fine, soil-like material. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's test is whether plants can grow in it.

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel stated a general rule:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁמְּגַדֵּל בּוֹ צְמָחִים – מְכַסִּין בּוֹ,
phrases.english: Something in which plants grow, one may cover with it,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְגַדֵּל צְמָחִים – אֵין מְכַסִּין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: and something in which plants do not grow, one may not cover with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a general rule in place of the משנה's list in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that plants can grow in may be used to cover the blood; anything else may not.

steps.title: What counts as 'fine sand'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of 'fine sand' from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is 'fine sand'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking what the משנה means by 'fine sand'. It is setting up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows 'fine sand' but forbids 'coarse sand' without saying where the line is. The גמרא wants a clear way to tell the two apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא – the discussion on the משנה starts here
'What is it like?' – asking for a clear definition
Fine sand

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is considered fine sand?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a word in the משנה of Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the line is between 'fine sand' (allowed) and 'coarse sand' (not allowed).

steps.title: Fine sand is sand a potter does not need to crush
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן defines fine sand as any sand that a potter does not need to crush before using it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Fine sand is any sand that the potter does not need to crush.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers with a practical test: look at how a potter would treat the sand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A potter crushes sand that is too lumpy to use. So if the sand is already fine enough for him to use as it is, it counts as 'fine sand' and may be used to cover the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: A potter, someone who makes clay vessels
To crush it
Anything that; any case where

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Any sand that the potter does not need to crush.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Fine sand is any sand a potter does not need to crush.

steps.title: A second version: רבי יוחנן was defining 'coarse sand'
steps.stepSummary: Some teach רבי יוחנן's statement on the later part of the משנה: coarse sand is any sand that a potter must crush.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this on the later part of the משנה: 'But one may not cover with coarse manure or coarse sand.' What is coarse sand? רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Any sand that the potter needs to crush.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same teaching. In this version, רבי יוחנן was defining the forbidden 'coarse sand', not the allowed 'fine sand'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is the same in both versions: whether a potter needs to crush the sand. What changes is which part of the משנה רבי יוחנן was explaining. In this version, he was defining the sand that may not be used, instead of the sand that may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Some teach it' – introduces a second version of a teaching
On the later part (of the משנה)
Coarse, lumpy sand

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions use the potter test. The first version uses it to define the allowed 'fine sand'; the second uses it to define the forbidden 'coarse sand'.

phrases.english: And some teach it on the later part of the משנה:

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין מְכַסִּין לֹא בְּזֶבֶל הַגַּס
phrases.english: "But one may not cover with coarse manure
nor with coarse sand."
What is considered coarse sand?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Any sand that the potter needs to crush.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of Steps 14-15, attaching רבי יוחנן's definition to the later part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, coarse sand, which may not be used for covering, is any sand a potter needs to crush.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two versions of רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just brought two versions of רבי יוחנן's statement. Now it asks whether they lead to any different result in a real case. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One version defines fine sand as sand a potter does not need to crush. The other defines coarse sand as sand a potter must crush. At first these look like two sides of the same coin, so the גמרא wants to know if they ever give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? The standard question asking for the practical difference between two opinions or versions.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the two versions of רבי יוחנן's statement from the last two steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two versions of רבי יוחנן's statement (steps 15 and 16) differ in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two versions of רבי יוחנן's definition give different rulings.

steps.title: The difference is sand that only crumbles by hand
steps.stepSummary: The two versions differ about sand that needs some crushing but not real crushing, meaning it just crumbles in the hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them regarding sand that needs and does not need crushing, meaning sand that crumbles by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The two versions disagree about in-between sand that you can crumble with your fingers without a tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first version, only sand that needs real crushing is excluded. Crumbly sand does not really "need crushing," so it may be used to cover the blood. Under the second version, any sand that needs some crushing counts as coarse, so crumbly sand may not be used.

keyTerms.meaning: Needs and does not need. Here it means an in-between case that needs a little crushing but not full crushing.
It crumbles easily, falling apart in the hand without a tool.

steps.whatToRemember: Sand that only crumbles by hand is allowed under the first version of רבי יוחנן and not allowed under the second version.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them regarding sand that needs and does not need crushing,
phrases.notes: It "needs" a little crushing, but it "doesn't need" the real crushing a potter does with a tool.

phrases.english: meaning, sand that simply crumbles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sand that only crumbles by hand is allowed under the first version and not allowed under the second.

steps.title: The פסוק excludes stones and an upside-down vessel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word "בֶּעָפָר" that the blood may not be covered with stones or by turning a vessel over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "And cover it." You might think he may cover it with stones or turn a vessel over it. So the פסוק says: "with earth."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads the פסוק about כיסוי הדם. It shows that "covering" must be done with earth, not with stones or an upside-down vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "וְכִסָּהוּ" alone might suggest that any way of hiding the blood works. The extra word "בֶּעָפָר" limits it to earth-like material. This is the source for the ruling in the משנה about stones and an upside-down vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: "You might think." It opens a possible mistaken reading that the פסוק will rule out.
"The פסוק teaches us." It introduces the words of the פסוק that settle the question.
"With earth." The word in the פסוק that sets which material is used for covering.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the תורה source behind the משנה's rule that stones and an upside-down vessel are not valid for כיסוי הדם.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "And cover it"
You might think he may cover it with stones
or turn the vessel over it?
So the verse says: "with earth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that gives the פסוק source for the משנה's rules (Step 12) on valid and invalid covering materials. It continues the same topic of covering materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Covering must be done with earth. Stones or an upside-down vessel do not work.

steps.title: Which other fine materials are included beyond earth?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that fine manure, fine sand, crushed stones, crushed pottery and fine flax chaff may also be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about earth. From where do we include fine manure, fine sand, crushed stones, crushed pottery, and fine flax chaff?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and asks how we know that other fine materials, not just earth, may be used for covering. The answer comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "בֶּעָפָר" alone could mean only real earth. The ברייתא wants a source that widens the rule to other fine materials that act like earth. These match the fine materials listed as valid in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: "I only have." It means the פסוק so far teaches only this one case.
"From where do we include?" It asks for a source that adds more cases.
The fine chaff shaken off flax when it is beaten.

phrases.english: I only know about earth;
from where do we include fine manure,
fine sand, crushed stones,
crushed pottery,
fine flax chaff,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא עָפָר, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After limiting covering to earth, the ברייתא asks for a source that widens the rule to other fine materials.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source from the פסוק that includes fine materials besides earth for כיסוי הדם.
